name: Karan Kunjur
current_role: CEO and Co-Founder, K2 Space (Torrance, California)
profile: Karan Kunjur co-founded K2 Space with CTO Neel Kunjur (ex-SpaceX Dragon avionics) to build very large, high-power satellites, betting against the industry trend toward small sats. K2 raised a $110M Series B in early 2025, opened a Seattle-area engineering office and in July 2026 launched Gravitas, billed as one of the highest-powered spacecraft ever built.
interesting_fact: K2's pitch, in its CTO's words: 'The industry went small. We asked: what happens if you go the other way?' Its stated long-term aim is space infrastructure for a 'Type II civilization'.
deep_cut_fact: Before space, he spent about 10 years at BCG and then helped lead an AI startup from seed stage to a nine-figure exit.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast angle (high-power satellites, space-based infrastructure).

name: Matteo Franceschetti
profile: Matteo Franceschetti co-founded Eight Sleep in 2014 with Massimo Andreasi Bassi, Andrea Ballarini and Alexandra Zatarain. Eight Sleep sells the Pod, a temperature-regulating 'sleep fitness' mattress cover that tracks heart rate and breathing; it started with a 2015 crowdfunding campaign and is backed by Valor, SoftBank and Founders Fund.
interesting_fact: He came to sleep via sport: 'I was into the idea of sleep as recovery... That is how we came up with the idea of sleep fitness.' His stated vision is to 'compress your sleep and save your life.'
deep_cut_fact: The company was originally called just 'Eight', a reference to the fabled eight hours of sleep, though he argues a good six hours beats eight poor ones.
notes: Active on X under @m_franceschetti; Eight Sleep press page also offers a downloadable press kit.
